webster.text: A pleasing deportment; courtesy; that manner of address and behaviour in social intercourse which gives pleasure; civility; obliging condescension; kind and affable reception and treatment of guests; exterior acts of civility; as, the gentleman received us with complaisance.

more.text: Desire of pleasing; disposition to oblige; the principle for the act.

example.quote: To this reasoning it has been objected that the President, by the influence of the power of nomination, may secure the complaisance of the Senate to his views.
